subject: Spanska 3
title: Relative clauses: que, quien, donde and cuyo
sourceSummary: How to build more advanced descriptive sentences using relative pronouns: que, quien, donde and cuyo.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun: "El hombre ___ vive al lado es profesor."
questions.opener: "Que" is the most general relative pronoun and works for both things and people as a subject.
questions.explanation: "Que" is used as the subject in restrictive relative clauses for both people and things: "el hombre que vive..." (the man who lives...). "Quien" would have required a comma or a preposition before it in this context.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun: "La mujer con ___ hablé ayer es mi tía."
questions.opener: After a preposition (con, de, a, para) referring to a person, "quien" is usually used, not "que".
questions.explanation: After preposition + a person, "quien" (or "quienes" in the plural) is used: "con quien hablé" (who I talked to). "Que" is rarely used directly after a preposition when it refers to a person.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun: "Esta es la casa ___ nací."
questions.opener: When it's about a place, "donde" can replace "en la que".
questions.explanation: "Donde" is used for places and corresponds to "en la que/en el que": "la casa donde nací" = "la casa en la que nací" (the house where I was born).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "El escritor ___ libros son famosos ganó un premio."
questions.opener: "Cuyo" agrees with the word that comes AFTER it (the thing owned), not with the owner.
questions.explanation: "Cuyo" functions as a possessive adjective and agrees in gender/number with the thing owned — here "libros" (masculine, plural) → "cuyos". The owner ("el escritor") doesn't affect the form.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly combines the two sentences: "Tengo un amigo. Mi amigo vive en Perú."?
questions.opener: Which relative pronoun replaces "mi amigo" as the subject of the second clause?
choices: Tengo un amigo que vive en Perú.
Tengo un amigo quien vive en Perú.
Tengo un amigo donde vive en Perú.
Tengo un amigo cuyo vive en Perú.
questions.explanation: "Que" is the default choice as the subject of a restrictive relative clause, whether it refers to people or things: "un amigo que vive en Perú". "Quien" as the subject of a restrictive clause without a comma isn't correct here.

questions.prompt: When MUST you use "quien" instead of "que"?
questions.opener: Think about prepositions: con, a, de, para...
choices: Always when it refers to people
After a preposition, when it refers to a person
questions.explanation: "Quien(es)" is required after a preposition when it refers to a person: "la persona a quien escribí", "el amigo con quien viajé". Elsewhere, especially as a subject, "que" is usually the natural choice even for people.

questions.prompt: Find and correct the two errors: "El pueblo cual visité el verano pasado es precioso, y la señora cuyo casa está en la plaza me invitó a tomar café."
questions.opener: One error concerns which relative pronoun to use as an object, the other concerns the agreement of "cuyo".
questions.answer: El pueblo que visité el verano pasado es precioso, y la señora cuya casa está en la plaza me invitó a tomar café.
steps: "cual" without an article (el/la cual) doesn't work as a standalone relative pronoun here — as the object of a restrictive clause, "que" is used: "el pueblo que visité".
"cuyo casa" is wrong because "cuyo" must agree with the word it precedes — "casa" is feminine, so it should be "cuya casa".
The full corrected sentence: "El pueblo que visité el verano pasado es precioso, y la señora cuya casa está en la plaza me invitó a tomar café."

questions.prompt: How are que, quien, donde and cuyo used?
questions.opener: Four relative pronouns, four different jobs.
questions.answer: que = the general relative pronoun, works for people and things, both as subject and object (el libro que leí, el hombre que vive aquí). quien/quienes = people only, required after a preposition (con quien, a quien) and common after a comma. donde = place, corresponds to en la que/en el que (la ciudad donde vivo). cuyo/cuya/cuyos/cuyas = possessive "whose", agrees with the thing owned, not with the owner (el autor cuyos libros...). Remember: cuyo is NOT the same as the question word ¿cuál?.
